issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/minimal-apis/overview with titles "Minimal APIs overview" / "Обзор minimal API"; link 1 is titled "Choose between controller-based APIs and minimal APIs"
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt shows that the minimal-apis/overview URL redirects to fundamentals/apis, and the page title is "APIs overview". So both links point to the same page. Neither title matches the real title, and "Minimal APIs overview" names a page that no longer exists as a separate page. A reader would see two different-looking sources that are one article.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep one link, fundamentals/apis, titled "APIs overview" (ru: "Обзор API"). If a second source is wanted, use a real distinct page, for example the Minimal APIs quick reference (fundamentals/minimal-apis) or fundamentals/minimal-apis/min-api-filters for endpoint filters and .NET 7. Update linkTitles in both locales so the count matches.

issues.claim: What controllers give you: MVC filters, ModelState, automatic 400 of [ApiController], extensible model binding, conventions and application parts; endpoint filters (AddEndpointFilter) introduced in .NET 7
issues.problem: The excerpt shows only a general statement that controllers may be preferred for "Applications requiring specific MVC features" and is cut off before any feature list. It does not confirm the controller-only features named, such as extensible model binding via IModelBinder and application parts. It also does not mention endpoint filters or .NET 7. From my own knowledge the claims are broadly correct, but the cited page does not demonstrate them.
issues.suggestedFix: Cite the min-api-filters page for endpoint filters and the .NET 7 claim. Cite a page that shows the feature comparison for the MVC-only features, or reduce the list to what the cited page supports. Re-check against the .NET 10 text of fundamentals/apis.

issues.problem: "Церемоний" is a calque of "ceremony" and reads unnaturally in Russian.

issues.claim: вокруг него работают только `middleware` и фильтры конечных точек

issues.claim: application parts, extensible model binding, MVC filter types in a junior question
issues.problem: The reference answer is deeper than junior (definitions and everyday use). It lists several MVC internals, which is more than a junior is expected to recall.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the answer, but make the junior core the first two bullets. Optionally shorten the "what controllers give you" bullet to MVC filters, ModelState and [ApiController] behaviour.

issues.problem: The fetched environments page contradicts itself. The table says "DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT, if present, ... takes precedence over ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT" for web apps. A later paragraph says "The ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT value overrides DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT" for WebApplication.CreateBuilder. The configuration page lists DOTNET_ above ASPNETCORE_ for WebApplicationBuilder host config. The excerpts therefore do not settle the precedence claim. The correct answer b/d does not depend on it.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the precedence parenthetical. For example: "`WebApplication.CreateBuilder` reads the environment name from the `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT` and `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` variables (for web apps you normally set `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`), and if neither is set it uses `Production`." Make the same change in ru.

issues.suggestedFix: en: "ASP.NET Core runtime environments"; ru: "Среды выполнения ASP.NET Core".

issues.claim: If `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` is not set, the app runs in the `Development` environment.
issues.problem: Option a is correctly false. Its wording could still be read as true when DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT=Development is set. The explanation for a does not mention that fallback, so the distractor is slightly ambiguous.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword a as "If no environment variable is set, the app runs in the Development environment". Optionally mention in optionExplanations.a that DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT can also supply the value.
